method: Two rounds of three fresh NEAR-only wallets; Phase 6D A/B and a Router with command timing. Diagnostic measurement, not a performance comparison.
limitations: Provider CPU and wall times describe whole invocations, not individual cryptographic operations.
Application clocks freeze during CPU work; application spans are not transport timers.
Small sequential samples do not establish a latency percentile or placement success rate.
D1 counts cover bound-root loads only; total Gateway D1 and backend Console calls are unavailable.
No diagnostic location fetches were added. Physical colocation is not proved.
Per-operation CPU profiles and internal payload-byte counts are unavailable.
Caller clocks can omit CPU time. Provider invocation wall time cannot be subtracted from caller duration to isolate network time exactly.
The Router operation label does not identify whether the live DO instance was newly constructed. Persistent prior state does not prove a warm instance.
interpretation: Router claim plus finish measured 832 ms median per registration (649–1154 ms). Claim dominated at 776 ms; finish was 56 ms. Claim DO wall time was 75 ms median. Dispatch, placement, or startup is a material hypothesis; the clocks do not isolate network latency. This was a diagnostic run, not a demonstrated speedup.
